note: Locked demo cases. Each prompt is phrased the way the advertised persona would actually type it - no operation names, no permit ids, no jargon a Permit Technician would not use. Cases were written from the one-pager's own capability bullets and pain statements, then tuned until the agent answered them cold.

cases.onepager_bullet: pain: long processing times and high citizen complaints
cases.prompt: Which permit applications have been sitting too long, and which resident is going to complain first?

cases.onepager_bullet: Classify and validate permit applications at intake
cases.prompt: Anything at the front counter I should not be accepting today?

cases.onepager_bullet: Route requests automatically to the correct review teams
cases.prompt: The restaurant fit-out on Harbor Way just came in. Who needs to review it and when is it due back?

cases.onepager_bullet: Centralize communication and provide instant updates to applicants
cases.prompt: My front desk is drowning in status calls. What can we send out today so people stop calling?

cases.onepager_bullet: Provide inspectors with mobile access and real-time assignments
cases.prompt: What inspections are on the board for the solar job, and who is covering them?

cases.onepager_bullet: Classify and validate permit applications at intake
cases.prompt: A new residential addition application just came in. Process it and tell me if it is complete.

cases.onepager_bullet: Classify and validate permit applications at intake
cases.prompt: Run the code compliance check on the Johnson addition plans.

cases.onepager_bullet: Route requests automatically to the correct review teams
cases.prompt: Route the Johnson addition for expert plan review.

cases.onepager_bullet: Centralize communication and provide instant updates to applicants
cases.prompt: Track the approval workflow for the Johnson addition.

cases.onepager_bullet: Provide inspectors with mobile access and real-time assignments
cases.prompt: Show me the permit issuance package for the Johnson addition.

assertion_principle: The tool description and parameters are the ONLY context the Brainstem has about this agent. So: expects_agent proves the description was sufficient to route; must_include is asserted against the agent's own output (deterministic, never the model's prose); must_not_include catches stalls that prove the agent was never called. A routing failure is a defect in the description, not flakiness.
